description: NOVEL approach (user decision 2026-07-15): instead of DAGMC/MOAB or libMesh, implement outram-mc's unstructured-mesh geometry+tallies on the OpenFOAM **polyMesh** format. Reuse the polyMesh reader / cell-face topology already ported in outram-foam-basic-lib (OpenFOAM primitive + FV layer, Layers 1-4) rather than a new mesh backend — this bridges the CFD and Monte Carlo sides of OUTRAM PARK. Covers the unstructured-mesh-part-i/ii notebooks (unstructured_mesh_part_i/ii tests). Point-location + track-length tally binning over polyMesh cells; coupling-friendly for future MC<->CFD. This is a research contribution, document as such. TODO.
title: outram-mc: unstructured-mesh tallies via OpenFOAM polyMesh (novel; reuse outram-foam-basic-lib)

description: Port the remaining OpenMC quadric CSG surface types into outram-mc-libs geometry/surface.rs, which currently has only XPlane/YPlane/ZPlane/Sphere/ZCylinder. Add: general Plane (ax+by+cz=d), XCylinder, YCylinder, XCone, YCone, ZCone, and general Quadric. Each needs evaluate/normal/distance (ray-quadric intersection) + a SurfaceKind enum variant wired into all match arms (evaluate/sense/distance/normal/reflect/bc) + unit tests (sense, on-axis distance, reflection). Mirror OpenMC src/surface.cpp. Torus{X,Y,Z} deferred (quartic, not a quadric — separate follow-up).
title: outram-mc: port remaining CSG quadric surfaces (Plane, X/YCylinder, cones, Quadric)

description:
Surfaced 2026-08-14 while retiring scripts/kloc_accounting.py. An initial claim that 'scripts/ now holds no Python at all' was made and was WRONG -- a find had been truncated by head. The accurate position:

TRACKED FIRST-PARTY PYTHON REMAINING, all in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/dev/:
  gen_fluid.py, gen_incompressible.py, gen_mixture.py   -- read the gitignored upstream CoolProp JSON clone, emit Rust
  regen_all.py, regen_incompressible_all.py, regen_mixture_all.py  -- drivers over the above; regen_all.py also rewrites src/fluids/mod.rs and src/fluid.rs to wire every fluid into the Fluid enum
  gen_latex_doc.py  -- scaffolds a bite-sized LaTeX doc series under docs/latex/

WHY THIS IS A DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The hard rule covers DOCUMENTATION AND ACCOUNTING. Six of these are code generation, which is neither. gen_latex_doc.py scaffolds documentation and arguably is in scope. Porting the generators would also mean reading CoolProp's JSON schema in Rust, against a clone that is not in the repository -- the same shape as gen_aster_behaviour_registry.py, which was retired rather than ported for exactly that reason.

OPTIONS: (a) leave them, and say so explicitly in the rule's scope; (b) port gen_latex_doc.py only; (c) retire the generators the way the aster importer was, recording the procedure beside their output; (d) port all seven.

NOT IN SCOPE EITHER WAY: */upstream_source/*.py (NJOY2016, Blender, TRISO-ATOPS vendored source) and collaboration/*.py (gitignored scratch).

ALSO WORTH DOING: scripts/vendor/ is now orphaned. It is gitignored and holds clones the retired kloc script made; kovan kloc vendors into its own output directory, so it can be deleted.
title: coolprop dev/*.py: decide whether the no-Python rule reaches them

description:
RESEARCH DIRECTION, deliberately deferred. Do not start before op-ku5q / gh:#194 is closed. Recorded on gh:#194 as a follow-on comment.

ORIGIN. Maintainer observation 2026-09-13: for resonances a frequency-domain representation beats resolving the lineshape on a grid, and windowed multipole is that move for sigma(E) - Reich-Moore cross sections are rational in sqrt(E), so sigma(E)*E is a sum of simple poles, each pole being a resonance at complex energy E_r - i*Gamma/2, and Doppler broadening becomes ANALYTIC through the Faddeeva function. src/gpu_wmp.rs already implements this (48-term Weideman w(z) per pole), so one dataset serves all temperatures with no BROADR pass.

WHY IT DOES NOT APPLY TO op-ku5q. Multipole represents sigma(E), a 1-D function. The op-ku5q defect is in P(E->E',mu), a transfer distribution. Different object; multipole says nothing about it.

WHAT DOES APPLY. The frequency-domain object underneath S(alpha,beta) is the phonon density of states rho(omega), and the machinery is already ported:
  crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/frequency.rs - 'Given a tabulated phonon
    frequency spectrum rho(E) on an evenly spaced energy grid, this builds
    everything the phonon expansion needs at one temperature' (ports start, fsum)
  crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/continuous.rs - the incoherent-Gaussian
    phonon expansion S(alpha,-beta) = e^{-alpha lambda} sum_n (alpha lambda)^n/n!
    * T_n(beta), with T_{n+1} = T_1 * T_n by self-convolution (ports contin,
    terpt, convol); SCT tail fill at large alpha where the sum has not converged

PROPOSAL. Sample the outgoing energy and angle from the phonon expansion directly, rather than from a tabulation of a tabulation of S. Same principle as multipole: work where the physics is sparse instead of resolving its consequences on a grid. Comparable to on-the-fly thermal scattering in OpenMC / Serpent.

OPEN QUESTIONS BEFORE IT IS WORTH ANYTHING: truncation of the phonon sum per sample; the SCT tail fill at large alpha; cost per scatter against the current ~10 Msample/s; whether coherent elastic (Bragg) still needs its own path; and whether detailed balance holds exactly in the sampler rather than only in the tabulated law.

HARD CONDITION. Must be PRICED against the same NJOY THERMR oracle as everything else in this hunt (examples/graphite_kernel_vs_njoy_thermr.rs, h2o_kernel_vs_njoy_thermr.rs), not adopted on the strength of being the more principled representation. Being structurally correct is not evidence - that is the standing lesson of gh:#193.
title: outram-mc: sample thermal scatters from the LEAPR phonon expansion instead of a re-binned S(alpha,beta) tabulation

description: bedok-yan-ren (merged into develop 2026-08-17, commit e189633641) replaced the src/reference/{nodal,th,cases,coupling} architecture (~14.5k lines) with ~30 flat one-file-per-.m modules (calc_*.rs, sanodaldiffusion_solverxyz.rs, etc.), and deleted the prior integration/benchmark/parity test suite: tests/benchmark/main.rs, tests/parity/main.rs, tests/fixture_loading.rs, tests/support/mod.rs, and the IAEA-3D fixture data. CORRECTION: the flat modules do carry inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests (153 of them, verified via 'cargo test --release -p bedok --lib --tests'), so coverage is not zero -- what's missing is integration-level/benchmark coverage. 2 of the 153 tests are FAILING as merged: sanodaldiffusion_solverxyz::tests::a_warm_start_does_not_reliably_reduce_the_iteration_count and sanodaldiffusion_solverxyz::tests::the_debug_diagnostics_are_gated_and_carry_the_references_nan (panic at src/sanodaldiffusion_solverxyz.rs:1094 and :936). bedok is now Yan Ren's crate (he works in bedok-yan-ren; maintainer merges periodically) -- these failures are his to triage, not ours to silently fix. Still needed: a decision with Yan Ren on whether/how to restore integration/benchmark coverage (previously #[ignore]d NEACRP/IAEA-3D gates that were never actually run, per docs/melcor-parity-scoping.md and docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md section 1.3, both now removed) against the new flat layout.
title: bedok: rebuild test coverage after Yan Ren's flat-module rewrite
